Reverse osmosis drinking water systems

A reverse osmosis (RO) system sits under your kitchen sink and gives you clean drinking water from its own faucet. It’s the most thorough option for the water you drink and cook with.

Book a free water test Call 734-878-2572

What it removes

RO reduces a wide range of contaminants, including:

  • Lead and other heavy metals
  • Arsenic and nitrates
  • Dissolved solids, sediment and cysts
  • Bacteria and many chemicals, including pesticides
  • Chlorine taste and odor

How it works

Water is pushed under pressure through a series of filters:

  1. Pre-filter. Catches larger particles, chlorine and other substances that would damage the membrane.
  2. Membrane. A semi-permeable membrane lets water through and holds back finer contaminants.
  3. Carbon filter. Activated carbon takes care of any remaining taste and odor.

The clean water is stored in a small tank and comes out of a dedicated faucet at your sink, so it’s there when you want it.

Upkeep

The pre-filter, membrane and carbon filter need replacing from time to time. How often depends on your water and how much you use. Dan can set a schedule for your system and do the filter changes for you.

On hard or iron water, a softener or iron filter ahead of the RO helps protect the membrane.

Common questions

How often should I replace the filters?

It depends on your water quality and how much you use. Dan can look at your system and give you a replacement schedule.

Can I install an RO system myself?

An RO install means precise plumbing connections and adjustments, and some manufacturers void the warranty if it isn’t installed by a professional.

Is reverse osmosis the most effective filter?

For drinking water, it removes the widest range of contaminants. It treats the water at one faucet, though, not the whole house. For whole-house problems, see softeners, iron filters and filtration.
